metadata.summary: Explore the four stages of a butterfly's life: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and adult butterfly.
objectives: Identify the four stages of a butterfly life cycle.
Order the stages from egg to adult butterfly.
Explain that a chrysalis is the pupa stage before the adult butterfly.
Explain that an adult female butterfly lays an egg to begin a new cycle.
metadata.scopeNote: This lesson names the common four-stage butterfly life cycle without adding species-specific timing, egg counts, host plants, or other details.

answers.explanation: The life cycle starts with an egg.

questions.prompt: Which order shows the life cycle?
What comes out of the chrysalis?

answers.explanation: The adult butterfly emerges from the chrysalis.

questions.prompt: How does a new cycle begin?

answers.text: An adult female lays an egg
answers.explanation: The new egg begins another life cycle.

questions.prompt: Which stage is right before the adult butterfly?

answers.explanation: The chrysalis, or pupa, comes before the adult butterfly.

objects.label: Butterfly life cycle world
objects.description: A persistent procedural scene with a plant and the four butterfly stages.

objects.label: Plant
objects.description: The quiet plant that holds the leaves and twig.

objects.label: Twig
objects.description: A twig near the top center where the chrysalis is attached.

objects.label: First leaf
objects.description: The lower-left leaf that holds the first egg.

objects.label: Second leaf
objects.description: The lower-right leaf that holds the new egg.

objects.label: Egg
objects.description: A small ribbed egg on the first leaf.

objects.label: Caterpillar (larva)
objects.description: A segmented caterpillar, also called the larva stage.

objects.label: Chrysalis (pupa)
objects.description: A ridged chrysalis, also called the pupa stage, attached beneath the twig.

objects.label: Adult butterfly
objects.description: An adult butterfly with a body, antennae, legs, and rounded wing lobes.

objects.label: New egg
objects.description: A distinct new egg on the second leaf that starts another cycle.

steps.title: 1. Egg
steps.text: An adult female butterfly lays a tiny egg on a leaf. This egg is the first stage of the life cycle.
steps.alt: A small egg is shown on the first leaf at the lower left.
steps.simplificationNote: The word tiny helps children notice the stage without adding a species-specific egg size.

steps.title: 2. Caterpillar (larva)
steps.text: The egg hatches. A caterpillar comes out. Caterpillar is the child-friendly name for the larva stage.
steps.alt: A segmented caterpillar with a head and little legs is shown below the leaf.
steps.simplificationNote: Caterpillar and larva are introduced together so the scientific word is available without replacing the familiar word.

steps.title: 3. Chrysalis (pupa)
steps.text: The caterpillar forms a chrysalis. Chrysalis is the name for the pupa stage before the adult butterfly.
steps.alt: A ridged chrysalis hangs under the twig near the top center.
steps.simplificationNote: Chrysalis and pupa are introduced together as two names for the same stage.

steps.title: 4. Adult butterfly
steps.text: An adult butterfly emerges from the chrysalis. This is the fourth stage of the life cycle.
steps.alt: An adult butterfly with rounded wings, antennae, and legs is shown at the center.
steps.simplificationNote: The visible body parts are named without adding details that are not needed for the cycle objective.

steps.title: 5. New cycle recap
steps.text: An adult female butterfly lays a distinct new egg on a second leaf. Remember the four stages: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and adult butterfly.
steps.alt: The adult butterfly and a distinct new egg on the second leaf show how the four-stage cycle starts again.
steps.simplificationNote: The final step recaps all four stages and shows a distinct new egg without claiming a timing or egg count.

accessibility.summary: A readable five-step lesson shows an egg on a leaf, a caterpillar, a chrysalis under a twig, an adult butterfly, and a new egg that begins the cycle again.
